name: Argentina
summary_text: Argentina has one of the world's most progressive legal frameworks — the 2012 Gender Identity Law allows administrative self-identification (no medical requirements), offers an X marker for non-binary people, and funds transition healthcare. Buenos Aires is "one of the safest major cities in Latin America for LGBTQ+ visitors." But the situation is deteriorating sharply under the Milei government: the president has called "gender ideology" "child abuse," issued decrees modifying the Gender Identity Law, and hate crimes hit a record 227 in 2025 (up 62%, one every 38 hours — trans women bearing the brunt). Police institutional violence against trans and travesti women is documented (arbitrary raids, drug-law criminalisation, searches only on travestis). The violence targets local vulnerable communities rather than tourists, but the trajectory is concerning. The 2012 self-ID law remains in force for adults and courts are pushing back on the Milei decrees.

sources.title: Argentina's transgender community confronts 'chaotic, desperate' situation
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Apr 2025): 'Argentina's transgender community confronts a 'chaotic, desperate' situation' under the Milei government — rollback of trans health and recognition policies amid rising hostility.

sources.title: Crímenes de odio en Argentina: aumento y récord de uno cada 38 horas - Agencia Presentes
sources.claim_summary: Agencia Presentes (Mar 2026, Spanish): 'Hate crimes in Argentina: increase and a record of one every 38 hours' — the National Observatory of LGBT+ Hate Crimes recorded 227 hate crimes in 2025, a record — on average one every 38 hours.

sources.title: Argentina | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Argentina was long a regional leader - first Latin American country to legalise marriage equality (2010) and one of the world's most progressive gender identity laws (2012, legal gender change without medical procedures or judicial approval), with nonbinary markers recognised and trans employment quotas. Since Milei took office in December 2023, documented rollbacks include elimination of the Ministry of Women, Gender and Diversity and closure of the anti-discrimination institute.

misterb&b gay travel guide to Buenos Aires safety (2026): describes Buenos Aires as one of the safest major cities in Latin America for LGBTQ+ visitors, citing the 2010 marriage law and 2012 self-ID gender law; same-sex couples holding hands in Palermo, Recoleta and San Telmo draw no particular reaction. Travel-oriented, gay-male-focused perspective.

sources.title: Gender Identity Law (Argentina) - Wikipedia
sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia article on Argentina's Gender Identity Law (Law 26,743, effective June 2012): allows transgender people to be treated according to their self-perceived gender identity in government documents and healthcare, without requiring surgery, diagnosis or judicial approval - the first law of its kind globally.

sources.title: La Corte Suprema dejó firme la condena a perpetua por el crimen de la activista trans Diana Sacayán - Infobae
sources.claim_summary: Infobae (April 2025, in Spanish): Argentina's Supreme Court upheld the life sentence of the murderer of trans activist Diana Sacayán (killed 2015), declining to reinstate the 'travesticidio' hate-based aggravating factor that lower courts had removed - a signal about how hate-motive recognition for anti-trans killings is contested in the courts.

CNN (Nov 2009): Buenos Aires mayor Mauricio Macri declined to appeal a court ruling legalising same-sex marriage in the capital ('the world is headed in that direction'); the court found the civil-code articles restricting marriage to different-sex couples illegal; same-sex unions remained illegal in most of Argentina at the time - prelude to the 2010 national law.
